claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children that you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. We live in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation:

**Are you responsible for Alex's day-to-day care? For example, do you provide for his food, clothes, and other needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for all of his day-to-day care - his meals, clothes, school things, everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. A few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's actually a bit of a situation. Alex's other parent and I are both responsible for him, but we can't agree on who should claim the Child Benefit. We're both involved in his care, but we haven't been able to sort out between us who should be the one to claim it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. This is an important detail. Let me ask a clarifying question:

**Does Alex live with you full-time, or does he split his time between you and his other parent? And if he splits his time, approximately how much time does he spend with each of you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with me full-time. He's at my house all the time - that's where he goes to school from, where he sleeps every night, all of that. His other parent is involved in his life, but Alex lives with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have enough information now to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Result: **ELIGIBLE**

Good news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

✓ Alex is 8 years old (under 16)  
✓ You live in the UK  
✓ Alex lives with you full-time  
✓ You're responsible for his day-to-day care and expenses

**Important point about the disagreement with Alex's other parent:**

The rules state that only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child. While you and Alex's other parent haven't agreed on who should claim, the fact that Alex lives with you full-time and you provide all his day-to-day care strongly supports your claim.

If both of you were to apply for Child Benefit for Alex, HMRC would make the decision about who receives it. Given that Alex lives with you full-time, you have a strong case.

**One more thing to be aware of:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you can still claim the benefit.

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit for Alex!
